indicator_researcher: The next setting follows the last result. A change that raises profit, without a higher drawdown, is increased again until the drawdown rises or the profit falls by 5 percent. The stop and the take profit are inputs and are moved along with every other input. One input changes per run, and that change is the label on the result. A strategy is filed when the drawdown stays inside $2,500 until the profit passes $3,000, then $2,500 plus 30 percent of the profit above $3,000, the run has at least 60 trades, profit is above $6,000, the profit factor is above 1.1, and the win rate is above 40 percent. Those are the boxes turned on at the strategy library page. That is $115 a week and about 1.2 trades a week at a steady pace. The 7, 30, and 90-day tests need more than $115, $485, and $1,477 profit and at least 2, 5, and 15 trades. It must also make more than its drawdown, trade no more than 600 times a year, make more profit on each of the last 7, 30, 90, and 365 days than on the shorter window before it, and the stop may not be set above 1.5 percent of the account. A fill past that stop does not count against it. Two or three trades is not a strategy. Among the stored runs, the lower drawdown still ranks first and the larger profit after that. The best version uses desk_cooldown_bars=0, desk_daily_loss=1, desk_daily_profit=0, desk_max_trades_day=1, entry_end_hr=14, entry_end_mn=16, eod_hr=7, eod_mn=45. Attempts recorded: 51.
